\[
\boxed{(S_p,E_p,K_p)=\left(3,\,1,\,\frac{(p-1)^3}{2}\right)}
\]

Let \(D=k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\). An invertible distributive law between two copies is determined by the image of \(\varepsilon_j\otimes \varepsilon_i\). Writing the resulting algebra with generators \(x_i,x_j\), \(x_i^2=x_j^2=0\), the relation must have the form
\[
x_jx_i=a_{ij}+d_{ij}x_ix_j.
\]
The twisting conditions force
\[
a_{ij}=0 \quad\text{or}\quad d_{ij}=-1,
\]
with \(d_{ij}\ne 0\). Thus if \(a_{ij}\ne0\), then
\[
x_jx_i=a_{ij}-x_ix_j,
\]
and the pair algebra is isomorphic to \(M_2(k)\), hence simple. If \(a_{ij}=0\), the pair algebra is not simple. Therefore \(s(\Lambda)\) is the number of nonzero \(a_{ij}\)’s.

For three labels, the Yang-Baxter equation on \(x_3\otimes x_2\otimes x_1\) gives exactly
\[
a_{23}(d_{12}d_{13}-1)=0,\qquad
a_{13}(d_{12}-d_{23})=0,\qquad
a_{12}(1-d_{23}d_{13})=0.
\]
Taking all three \(a_{12},a_{13},a_{23}\ne0\) forces
\[
d_{12}=d_{13}=d_{23}=-1,
\]
and then all three equations hold. Hence
\[
S_p=3.
\]

Among these maximizers, the total algebra has generators \(x_1,x_2,x_3\) with
\[
x_i^2=0,\qquad x_jx_i+x_ix_j=a_{ij}\quad(i<j),
\]
where all \(a_{ij}\in k^\times\). This is the Clifford algebra of the symmetric form with Gram matrix
\[
G=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&a_{12}&a_{13}\\
a_{12}&0&a_{23}\\
a_{13}&a_{23}&0
\end{pmatrix},
\]
whose determinant is
\[
\det G=2a_{12}a_{13}a_{23}\ne0.
\]
For a nondegenerate \(3\)-dimensional Clifford algebra over \(k\), the center is quadratic:
\[
Z(A_\Lambda)\cong k[t]/\left(t^2+\frac{\det G}{8}\right)
= k[t]/\left(t^2+\frac{a_{12}a_{13}a_{23}}4\right).
\]
Thus the center is a field exactly when \(-a_{12}a_{13}a_{23}\) is a nonsquare in \(k^\times\). In that case \(A_\Lambda\) has one primitive central idempotent. If it is a square, the center splits as \(k\times k\), giving two primitive central idempotents. Therefore the minimum possible value is
\[
E_p=1.
\]

Finally, for \((a_{12},a_{13},a_{23})\in(k^\times)^3\), exactly half have \(-a_{12}a_{13}a_{23}\) nonsquare. Hence
\[
K_p=\frac{(p-1)^3}{2}.
\]

So the exact answer is
\[
\boxed{\left(3,\,1,\,\frac{(p-1)^3}{2}\right)}.
\]
